A node is central if its distance to the other nodes in the network is short.31 Google’s PageRank is a query-independent algorithm that measures the static ranking of websites and is based on rank prestige.10 PageRank35 is a variant of eigenvector centrality, and is based on the idea that highly ranked web pages are linked to other highly ranked web pages.7 Eigenvector centrality, or prestige score, is a measure in graph theory that explains a node’s influence in a network.36 The purpose of the eigenvector centrality measure is to locate the most central nodes in the network.32 The eigenvector centrality of a node is influenced not only by the number of links that point to the node in question, but also by the prestige of the nodes connected to it.5 Alternatively, eigenvector centrality is a recursive way to define importance in networks and represents a form of directed network in which “in-links” denote greater power.29 Eigenvector centrality is determined by the largest characteristic eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix.27 If the centrality of vertex i is designated as x, the effect of prestige is accounted for by i making x proportional to the average of the centralities of the network neighbors of i, where t is i a vertex linked to vertex i; see equation (6). 1 (6) 𝑥 = ∑ 0 689(0) 7 where 𝛌 is an eigenvalue constant and M(i) is a set of neighbors of v.
